documents.title: Gynecology discharge summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Admitted: 3/6/2025. Discharged: 3/10/2025.
Diagnosis: acute pelvic inflammatory disease with right tubo-ovarian abscess.

Presentation: 35-year-old with three days of fever, lower abdominal pain on both sides that worsens with movement, and vaginal discharge. Prior chlamydia, most recently treated six months ago, and recent chancroid. Past injection drug use; ITP in remission.

On arrival: T 38.7 C (101.7 F), HR 110, BP 100/60. Cervical motion tenderness, tenderness of both adnexa, purulent discharge from the cervix.
Labs: WBC 15.0, Hgb 12.2, CRP 24 mg/L. Urine hCG negative. GC/CT NAAT negative; HIV nonreactive.
Pelvic ultrasound: complex multiloculated right adnexal mass with thick walls and internal debris, 5.4 x 4.6 x 4.1 cm.

Course: IV ceftriaxone, doxycycline and metronidazole. Afebrile within 48 hours, pain steadily improving, tolerating diet. Abscess size suitable for antibiotic therapy alone; no drainage or surgery required. Transitioned to oral therapy on day 4.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and metronidazole 500 mg twice daily to complete 14 days total.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; gynecology with repeat pelvic ultrasound in about 6 weeks. Partner treatment advised.
Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 3/6-3/10 for PID with a 5.4 cm right TOA, treated with IV then oral antibiotics, no drainage. Discharge summary reviewed.

Today: no fever since day 2 in hospital. Lower belly 'sore, not sharp.' Discharge almost gone. On day 9 of 14 of doxycycline + metronidazole; mild nausea, eating fine. No alcohol.

Vitals normal, afebrile. Abdomen soft, mild lower tenderness, no guarding or rebound.

A/P
1. PID with TOA - improving on oral therapy. Finish all 14 days. Gyn ultrasound in ~6 wk (she has the appointment). Return precautions reviewed.
2. Partners: she says she has told the one she's still seeing to get treated.
3. STI prevention again - condoms; offered a harm-reduction referral, declined for now.
4. Smoking - unchanged.

conditions.label: Acute pelvic inflammatory disease with tubo-ovarian abscess

reports.text: Transvaginal technique. Uterus normal in size. Endometrium thin. Right ovary normal in size and appearance; no residual adnexal collection. Left ovary normal. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Interval resolution of the right adnexal collection. Normal ovaries.

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Visit 4/24/2025, follow-up after admission for PID with right TOA.

Completed 14 days of oral antibiotics. No pain, fever or discharge. Exam: no cervical motion or adnexal tenderness. Repeat ultrasound today: the right adnexal collection has resolved and both ovaries look normal.

No further gynecologic follow-up needed for this; routine cervical screening with you. We discussed contraception and condom use.

Allergies: NKDA.

OB/GYN

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36F, physical.

Interval: PID with right TOA 3/2025, antibiotics only, gyn ultrasound 4/2025 resolved. No pelvic pain since. Chancroid and chlamydia 9/2024, retest negative 12/2024. HSV - no recurrences she's noticed. ITP - platelets normal 5/2024.
Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: ~5 cig/day. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. Not working. Doesn't want to discuss partners in detail today; condoms 'mostly.'

ROS: negative. No bruising.
Vitals normal. PHQ-9 3.
Exam: well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck without nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without bruising, petechiae or lesions. Neuro grossly normal, gait normal. Pelvic deferred - no symptoms, co-test not due until 2027.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: flu today. CBC, BMP.
2. ITP in remission - CBC.
3. Cervical screening - next co-test 2027.
4. Tobacco - counseled; she'll call if she wants help quitting.
5. STI prevention - condoms, walk-in testing.
Return in one year.

documents.title: Neurology discharge summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Admitted: 3/4/2026. Discharged: 3/11/2026 to inpatient rehabilitation.
Principal diagnosis: acute transverse myelitis, thoracic.

History: 36-year-old woman with two days of worsening weakness in both legs and numbness from the umbilicus down. About two weeks earlier she had a flu-like illness that passed without treatment. No trauma; denies recent risky behavior. Background: ITP in remission, prior genital infections including PID with TOA 3/2025, past injection drug use. Smoker. NKDA.

Exam on admission: strength 3/5 throughout both lower extremities. Light touch and pinprick reduced below T10. Lower extremity reflexes brisk; Babinski sign present on both sides. Arms normal. Cranial nerves normal.

Workup: CBC, ESR and CMP normal. Urgent MRI of the spine: focal T2 hyperintense signal in the thoracic cord. MRI brain: normal. Lumbar puncture: CSF white cells 14 (lymphocyte predominant), protein 58 mg/dL, glucose normal; oligoclonal bands absent; CSF culture and viral PCR panel negative. Serum AQP4 and MOG antibodies negative. HIV and RPR negative.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily x 5 days. Bladder emptying normal on scans throughout.

At discharge: legs 4-/5, standing and walking short distances with a walker and assistance. Sensory level persists.
Discharge medications: none.
Disposition: acute inpatient rehabilitation. Neurology clinic follow-up in about 2 months.

Neurology

documents.title: Inpatient rehabilitation discharge summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Admitted 3/11/2026, discharged home 3/27/2026.
Diagnosis: impaired mobility after acute transverse myelitis (thoracic).

Daily physical and occupational therapy. Gains in transfers, standing balance and gait. Bladder and bowel function normal throughout.

At discharge: independent with transfers; walks household distances with a rolling walker; stairs with rail and supervision. Leg strength improving.
Equipment: rolling walker, shower chair.
Plan: outpatient PT 2-3 times a week; neurology follow-up as scheduled.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

documents.title: home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi its Kelly. Im home from the rehab place, walking with a walker. PT 3x a week starting this week. Neurology sees me in May. Do you need to see me? Getting rides is hard right now

documents.title: RE: home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad you're home - I read the hospital and rehab summaries. Neurology and PT are the main thing right now. I would still like to see you once you're steadier on your feet; when rides are easier, call or message and we'll find a time. MassHealth covers rides to appointments - the front desk can help set that up. Call sooner for fever, new weakness, or any trouble with your bladder or bowels.

documents.title: Neurology clinic follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Visit 5/20/2026, follow-up of acute transverse myelitis (admitted 3/4-3/11/2026, IV methylprednisolone, then inpatient rehab).

Steadily better with outpatient PT. Now walking with a cane outdoors, none at home. Bladder and bowels normal.

Exam: lower extremity strength 4+/5 on both sides. Sensory level has faded; patchy reduced pinprick below T10. Reflexes still brisk in the legs.

Impression: recovering acute transverse myelitis. Brain MRI, CSF bands and AQP4/MOG antibodies at admission were reassuring.
Plan: continue PT. Repeat MRI of the thoracic spine this summer. No new medication. Return in 4 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

Neurology
